lesson.subtitle: Lesson 11 -- Love It or Hate It
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Andrea Zanellato | Lesson 11 -- Love It or Hate It
lesson.grammar_point: verb + -ing after verbs of preference (enjoy, love, like, hate, don’t mind, can’t stand, avoid)

listenings.text: Hi, I'm Emma, and I'm an HR manager in Edinburgh. Every year we ask our people three questions. What do you enjoy doing at work? What do you hate doing? And what don't you mind doing? This year, two hundred people answered. The number one answer for enjoy was working with the team. The number one answer for hate was paperwork: nobody likes filling in forms. And the surprise? A lot of people don't mind working overtime, but only one or two days a month. So next year we are going to change the forms and make them shorter. Small changes, happy people.

Hello, I'm Oliver, and I'm a recruiter in London. I'm a people person, so I love meeting candidates and talking to people all day. I don't mind small talk, and I don't mind dealing with difficult questions. But I hate doing paperwork, and my pet peeve is candidates who arrive late without a message. On my day off, I avoid checking my emails. I enjoy cooking for my family, and I love walking in the countryside. That's how I unwind. On Monday, I'm ready again.
